issues.title: UET "group keying" gloss doesn't match UEC 1.0 (claims transport-layer reduction)
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
Actually found and reported by @ayourtch (Andrew Yourtchenko) in his review of the -03 draft set (Major finding [F09]):

Section 6.6 requires reporting "UET group keying state (transport-layer reduction support per UEC Spec 1.0)". In UEC 1.0, group keying is a Transport Security Sublayer (TSS) key-management mechanism with no effect on transfer volume; in-network / transport-layer collective reduction is not part of the 1.0 release. The required result field is unimplementable as written.

Verified directly against the UEC 1.0.2 specification PDF before fixing: "group key" (SDK) is a per-client key-derivation mechanism under the TSS Secure Domain / KDF machinery, unrelated to reduction.

Fix: deleted the false transfer-layer-reduction gloss, renamed the field to "TSS group-key encryption state", and replaced the false transfer-volume claim with the accurate framing (affects per-packet security processing overhead, not transfer volume).

issues.title: PFC Pause Event count includes X-ON frames
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
"PFC Pause Event" is defined as any PAUSE frame on a priority class. That includes zero-quanta X-ON frames, so a DUT that signals resume explicitly reports roughly twice the event rate of one that lets the pause timer expire. Not comparable.

Count non-zero quanta only.

Found by @ayourtch in his -03 review (F80).

issues.title: Generator message size range goes to 8 GB, which isn't possible
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
Table says 64 B to 8 GB. The RETH DMA Length field is 32 bits, so a single RDMA message tops out at 4 GB, and most implementations advertise 1-2 GB.

Cap it and say how larger transfers get composed.

Found by @ayourtch in his -03 review (F70).

pulls.title: Editorial pass: address Andrew Yourtchenko's review + acronym/inclusive-language cleanup
pulls.author: cpignata
pulls.body:
## Summary

Addresses the minor and editorial issues identified by Andrew Yourtchenko in his review of the draft set (-03), plus a broader editorial pass covering acronym consistency, inclusive language, and idnits hygiene.

- Fixed the META-ROCE and DCQCN-PAPER citations: verified against ACM DL/dblp and found the Meta paper's lead author is Adithya Gangidi (not Anirudh) and its real title omits "AI"; both entries were missing their venue and most co-authors
- Replaced retired MLPerf workload names (BERT, ResNet, GPT-3 175B) with a version-agnostic procedure that requires reporting the MLPerf Training version instead
- Renumbered Test Category 1A to close the numbering gap (categories now run 1-8)
- Fixed the JFI range (was stated two different ways in two places), the DSCP/AF31 mislabel ("class 31" instead of class 3, drop precedence 1), the malformed "Min Header Overhead" claim (a pre-payload offset presented as a minimum, excluding the mandatory ICRC+FCS trailer), improper cross-run percentile averaging, and a mischaracterized AllGather/AllReduce BusBW ratio (reduction is accelerator compute, not fabric overhead)
- Neutralized advocacy phrasing in the UET sections ("designed to replace", "Critical differentiator")
- Removed fragile section-number citations into an expired, withdrawn draft (draft-ietf-bmwg-evpntest-11)
- Fixed the abstract's idnits INVALID_ABSTRACT_SECTION_REF citation, a stray "1 million endpoints" claim (UEC's spec says "millions"), and Jain's Fairness Index's missing possessive
- Standardized multiplication notation to × and switched <=/>= to ≤/≥; centered all figures
- Reviewed for NIST IR 8366 inclusive-language guidance (replaced "hang" with "stop responding")
- Fixed an Acknowledgments wording mismatch with the companion drafts and added Andrew Yourtchenko's review credit

pulls.title: Fix one Major finding from Andrew Yourtchenko's review
pulls.author: cpignata
pulls.body:
## Summary

Fixes the Major finding from Andrew Yourtchenko's review of the -03 draft set that wasn't included in the earlier editorial PR (#26, already merged).

- UET "group keying" was described as "transport-layer reduction support per UEC Spec 1.0"; verified against the UEC 1.0.2 specification and found group keying (SDK) is a TSS key-derivation/encryption mechanism with no relation to in-network reduction, which is not part of the 1.0 release. Renamed the field to "TSS group-key encryption state" and removed the false transfer-volume claim. Closes #27

reviews.author: fcalabri
reviews.body:
Replaced the byte-accurate UET frame table in Appendix B with an explicitly schematic layering diagram; moved wire format specifics to normative reference to Section 4 of the UEC 1.0 Specification. Removed the incorrect 16-byte "UET Common Header", since it does not exist in the UEC Specification.

-Corrected the on-wire sublayer order from SES first then PDS (it was previously shown as SES after PDS). 

-Fixed the entropy description: The Entropy Value is contained within the UDP Source Port Number and varies per packet, NOT in a separate UET header field -- The Frame Table previously stated both simultaneously. Now cross referenced to the correct Entropy Value Definition in the Terminology Document; this will insure that all  documents are consistent.

-Revised the RoCEv2 vs. UET Comparison Table: removed two non-verifiable entries ("PSN (Extended)", and estimated pre-payload byte counts); revised the UET entropy-source entry; and described PDC's as being established via in-band mechanisms instead of "Connectionless." Clarified that CMS state is encoded within PDS fields while TSS adds Security Headers if enabled.
-Updated two outdated statements regarding UDP port 4793 registration pending status; port 4793 has been assigned by IANA to Ultra Ethernet Transport.

pulls.title: Third pass on Andrew's -03 review
pulls.author: cpignata
pulls.body:
Three more from Andrew's review on training:
- PFC Pause Event was counting X-ON resume frames, which roughly doubles the rate on DUTs that signal resume explicitly. Non-zero quanta only now. Closes #29
- Generator message range said 8 GB; the 32-bit RETH DMA Length caps a single message well below that. Capped at 2 GB with a note on composing larger transfers. Closes #30
- Split the LLM-BENCH row, which was also describing INFERENCE-BENCH, and added the missing TERMINOLOGY row. Retitled the table since the companion drafts aren't existing BMWG work. Left the MUST NOT where it was. Closes #31

Fernando's follow-up commits also cover the three issues he filed. Audited each item against the branches:

- T_dispatch now reads "per source-destination pair" in both terminology and inference, so they agree again. Closes #33
- DCQCN removed from the hop-by-hop list in all three Security Considerations; PFC and CBFC are named instead. Closes #34
- RETH, ImmDt, MHA and IRN added to the acronyms appendix; RT renamed TG; Appendix A moved UET/PDC/ROD to the 5.1 row; Primary-KPI row picked up TPS; IRN expanded. The cross-document numeric section citations are gone, and I took out the last internal one (Section 5.2 -> anchor) in the terminology PR. Closes #35

Note #33 and #35 are mostly fixed over in the terminology and inference repos, GitHub just can't auto-close across repos so they're linked here.

reviews.author: fcalabri
reviews.body:
- Introduction (F03/F06): "require lossless transport (via RoCEv2)" restated as
  "RDMA transport with negligible application-visible loss"; one sentence added on
  how each transport meets it (RoCEv2: lossless operation via PFC/ECN; UET:
  tolerates wire-level loss, recovers via retransmission/trimming). Aligns with
  the Zero Packet Loss definition in TERMINOLOGY; 

- Section 6.6 (F43): retitled "Link-Layer and Network-Layer Enhancement
  Benchmarks"; objective now labels LLR/CBFC link-layer and Packet Trimming
  network-layer, matching the TERMINOLOGY recategorization. Anchor unchanged, so existing cross-references resolve.

- Reporting item 4 (F43): "optional link-layer features" -> "optional features";
  the list is unchanged, the layer label was wrong for Packet Trimming.

- Appendix B (F03): "0 ppm (lossless)" split by transport: 0 ppm wire-level loss
  (lossless RoCEv2 profiles) vs. 0 ppm application-visible loss (UET). Table
  remains non-normative.

- Appendix E item 6 (F43): layer attribution corrected (LLR/PRI link-layer,
  Packet Trimming network-layer); "additional framing" -> "additional or
  modified framing" since trimming truncates packets rather than adding headers.
